objective: Read a bounded simplified header prefix into safe optional entries without evaluating the body.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Readonly traversal, while loops and optional dictionaries remain current TypeScript foundations.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Separating a text prefix from later data is practical parsing work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: First-separator handling, normalization and prototype-safe keys transfer to other text adapters.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A clearly bounded header-block exercise keeps the foundational parser objective focused.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Required absent lookups and __proto__ assignment can silently lose data or return inherited functions.

defects: The brief inaccurately described a complete HTTP response as beginning with headers rather than a start line.
Required Record return/type tests promised text for absent names.
Plain reference/junior dictionaries mishandled __proto__ or exposed inherited names.
The hint overstated split as invalid even when its remaining pieces are rejoined.
rationale: Describe a simplified header block rather than a full HTTP message parser. Rewrite return/scaffold/steps to Partial<Record<string,string>>, safe dictionaries and two corrected public optional-lookup expectations plus a missing-string rejection. Preserve exact first colon-space values, lowercase names, last duplicate winner, frozen inputs and no body evaluation. Four runtime assertions inspect prototype keys/missing inherited names, later separators/value whitespace, an unread body getter, independent empty bags and1000 headers. Add a readonly-input/general optional string-index check. Reference/junior use while/indexOf; final senior/alternative wrap fromEntries in a null-prototype output and adopt Partial after the old required-Record baseline. Target processed prefix units/count, excluding the body.

objective: Encode own query pairs with exact encodeURIComponent behavior and stable enumeration order.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Typed entry iteration and URI component encoding remain current JavaScript/TypeScript basics.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Building query strings is practical URL-adapter work.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Encoding modes, ownership and output-size costs transfer to other serializers.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded primitive entries keep the foundational destructuring/encoding objective focused.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Inherited parameters or substituted form encoding can silently change an intended URL.

defects: Own-key classes, Unicode/error semantics and numeric String conversion were implicit.
Junior repeatedly appended a growing string instead of the requested pair collection/destructured loop.
A for-in encoder with inherited parameters passed all old own-only cases.
rationale: Retain reference/senior and valid map/join alternative; rewrite junior to collect pairs with for-of destructuring and join once. Define frozen/null-prototype own enumerable entries, ignored inherited/Symbol/nonenumerable data, numeric ordering, all primitive Number string conversions, exact punctuation/UTF-8/%20 behavior and URIError propagation for lone surrogates. Four runtime assertions inspect ownership/prototype-like keys, accented/supplementary text and unescaped punctuation, nonfinite/signed-zero numbers, lone-surrogate key/value failures and1000 pairs. Add null-value rejection. Target total input key/value units plus pair count and bounded encoded output, not just number of properties. No URLSearchParams/form-encoding substitution is demanded.

objective: Group subjects under an exact finite type guard and one consistent optional-scope teaching grammar.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Literal tuples, type guards and finite Records remain current TypeScript patterns.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Grouping bounded subject text is practical changelog tooling.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Grammar boundaries, exact preservation and independent result state transfer to other text adapters.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Explicit simplified syntax fits the intermediate parser/guard exercise.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Inconsistent scope parsing can misclassify valid notes or accept malformed nested brackets.

defects: Reference/junior accepted nested scope parentheses unlike the senior regex.
The first-separator hint failed when a legitimate scope contained colon-space text, which the original senior accepted.
Mutable section independence, exact whitespace and bounds needed fuller coverage.
The original reference passed all old simple-scope examples.
rationale: Preserve the broad useful scope grammar: nonempty text without nested parentheses, including colons/colon-space. Manual reference/junior identify a closing scope bracket before its summary separator; original regex senior/full alternative remain valid. Clarify single-line bounded subjects, exact case/whitespace, nonempty summaries including spaces and later separators, whole malformed/unknown fallback and independent four-section arrays. Four runtime assertions inspect nested/unmatched scopes, valid colon scopes and whitespace-only scope/summary, exact three-type guard, source/tuple preservation and1000 ordered subjects. Add true/false guard narrowing with readonly subjects. The initial narrower no-colon draft was revised before approval; baseline selected a narrower regex on old simple fixtures, while the final accepted alternative restores the original full scope regex. Target total subject units/count, with fixed three-type membership constant work.
